The court will most likely declare the statute **unconstitutional as an equal protection violation that favors established parties**. The 20% rule gives parties automatic access through primaries, while independents must collect 7% of the electorate, the same kind of disparity struck down in *Williams v. Rhodes* (1968). This reverses my earlier answer, which put too much weight on *Jenness* and *Storer*, cases that involved neutral signature rules rather than a two-tier system favoring established parties.

CONFIDENCE: 70
